KASPARRO
Brand Engineer
Full-time · Bengaluru · On-site with evening flexible for US clients
Role
Brand Engineer
Team
Brand Engineering — reports to Founder
Type
Full-time
Experience
3–5 years in CS, implementation, AEO/SEO delivery, or solutions consulting
Location
HSR Layout, Bengaluru (on-site, some evening calls for US clients)
Compensation
₹12–15 LPA fixed + ₹3–5 LPA variable + ₹3–5 LPA ESOPs
Tools
Notion · Google Workspace · Slack · Loom · GSC · GA4 · Internal platform · AI Tools (ChatGPT, Claude)


ABOUT KASPARRO
Kasparro is an AI Visibility platform. We help brands get discovered, recommended, and chosen by AI engines — ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Mode. As buyers increasingly start their research inside AI assistants, being recommended (or ignored) by those engines becomes a commercial issue. That’s the gap we close.
We don’t just measure the problem — we fix it. Our engagement spans four product layers: monitoring and intelligence across AI engines, on-site technical fixes and content to make a brand’s owned surfaces machine-readable, off-site engagement to shape the narrative AI sees everywhere else (Reddit, reviews, YouTube, Wikipedia), and authority and citation building to earn the trust signals AI engines rely on. Each client gets a dedicated Brand Engineer who runs the full stack: strategy, brief creation, output QA, coordination with the client’s teams, and measurable outcomes.
We’re backed by experienced founders, CMOs, and angels. We’re small, fast-moving, and building quickly in HSR Layout, Bengaluru.

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
When a brand signs with Kasparro, they’re not buying a report. They’re buying a dedicated operator who understands their brand goals, diagnoses where they’re invisible or misrepresented by AI engines, drives the technical and content fixes that close those gaps, shapes how AI sees them across every off-site surface, tracks the outcomes, and expands the engagement as results land.
Today the founder plays that role for every client. That doesn’t scale. This role exists to be that operator — the Brand Engineer who owns the full client lifecycle from onboarding through ongoing delivery, outcomes, and expansion — and to build the delivery function as the client base grows.
The Brand Engineer writes the brief. The Kasparro platform and team generate the output — technical fixes, content, engagement plays, monitoring reports. The Brand Engineer QAs the output, delivers it to the client, coordinates implementation with the client’s agencies or internal teams, tracks what moved, and shapes the next month’s strategy based on the results.

WHAT THE WORK LOOKS LIKE
The client. VP Marketing, Head of E-commerce, Head of Growth, or founder — typically at companies doing $10M–$100M+ in revenue, spending $2M–$20M on digital marketing annually. US and India. These are people who bought Kasparro because they saw evidence that AI engines are ignoring or misrepresenting their brand — and understood the commercial impact. They’re data-literate, they run agencies or internal marketing and tech teams, and they expect you to be the single point of accountability for AI visibility across their brand.
The four product layers. Every engagement runs on a combination of monitoring and intelligence (how AI engines see the brand, tracked continuously), on-site fixes and content (making the brand’s owned surfaces — site, product pages, landing pages — machine-readable and extractable), off-site engagement (shaping how the brand is discussed on Reddit, Quora, YouTube, reviews, Wikipedia), and authority and citation building (earning the backlinks, press placements, and trust signals that AI engines rely on when forming recommendations). The mix and depth varies by client. You run all active layers for each account.
The workflow. You translate the client’s brand goals and visibility gaps into specific briefs — what pages need schema fixes, what content to create, which off-site surfaces to engage, what authority plays to run. The Kasparro platform and team generate the outputs from your briefs. You QA every output before it reaches the client. Then you deliver it, coordinate implementation with the client’s agencies or internal tech and marketing teams, measure what moved, and use the data to shape the next cycle.
The strategy layer. You run monthly strategy reviews with each client. You translate monitoring data into business language: where the brand is being recommended, where it’s being excluded, which competitors are displacing it, and what to fix next. When a VP Marketing at a $50M D2C brand asks “why are we losing the comparison to our top competitor?” — you show them the exact gaps in how AI engines see both brands, and you walk them through the fix plan.
The geography. US and India clients. Most US interactions are async — Loom walkthroughs, documented briefs, Slack. Live calls happen 1–3 evenings a week. India meetings are in-person or daytime video.

WHAT YOU OWN
Client delivery across all product layers. You run the monthly delivery cycle for each account: write the briefs, QA the outputs, deliver to the client, coordinate implementation, and track completion. Nothing slips. SLAs are yours — delivery timelines, response windows, follow-up cadence. The tracking system is always current.
Strategic client engagement. You don’t just deliver outputs — you run strategy. Monthly reviews where you translate monitoring data into prioritized actions based on the client’s brand goals. You shape what gets fixed this month, what content gets created, and which off-site surfaces get attention — and you explain why in terms of business outcomes, not technical jargon.
Brief writing and output QA. You write the briefs that drive every fix, content piece, and engagement play. The platform and team generate the outputs. You QA every output against the client’s brand voice, accuracy standards, and delivery checklist before it goes out. You’re the quality gate.
Agency and team coordination. Most clients have existing SEO, PR, content, or community agencies — or internal tech and marketing teams. You don’t replace them. You brief them on what needs to happen, provide the specifications, and track execution. You’re the intelligence and coordination layer; they’re the implementation arms.
Outcomes tracking and expansion. You own the scoreboard. The client’s AI visibility scores move (or don’t) based on what you drove. You track the relationship between fixes and outcomes, build the evidence case, and use that data to drive net revenue expansion — tier upgrades, new product layers, additional brand coverage. You don’t cold-sell; the data makes the case.
Voice of Customer and product feedback. You surface patterns to the founder, tech, and product teams: recurring client needs, delivery friction, feature gaps, and — critically — where agentic automation can replace manual work. When you notice the same brief type being written for every client, that’s an automation suggestion. When you see a QA step that AI tools could handle, you flag it with specifics.

YOUR FIRST 12 MONTHS
Month 1
Learn the product, the industry, and the client motion
Build your foundation in the fundamentals: how SEO and AEO work, what structured data and schema markup do, how Google Search Console and GA4 tie to organic and AI-referred traffic, and how AI visibility systems score and monitor brands across engines. Shadow the founder through a full client cycle — Brand Source of Truth lock, on-site technical fixes, content strategy, off-site engagement, monitoring. Run the platform on 3–5 brands yourself. Understand how the four product layers connect and how each one moves the client’s visibility scores.
Months 2–3
Own 5 accounts, drive the first fixes
Take over 5 client accounts end-to-end. Run monthly strategy reviews. Write the briefs that the Kasparro platform and team use to generate on-site fixes, content, and off-site engagement plays — then QA every output before it reaches the client. Coordinate with each client’s agencies or internal tech and marketing teams. Track which fixes are implemented, which are stuck, and what’s moving the scores. Target: zero SLA misses, first expansion conversation initiated.
Months 4–6
Scale to 10–15 accounts, build the system
You’re managing 10–15 accounts simultaneously across US and India. You’re running strategy calls, delivering monthly cycles across all product layers, and driving net revenue expansion — tier upgrades, new product additions, additional brand coverage. You’re producing weekly Voice of Customer briefs. You’re flagging to tech and product where agentic automation can replace manual work. You’re documenting every recurring workflow into a playbook. Clients ask for you by name.
Year 1+
Build the function
Lead Brand Engineer → Head of Client Success. You hire your first associate. You own delivery quality, SLAs, retention, expansion, and the product feedback loop across the entire client base. The function is yours.


WHO THIS IS FOR
You’ve done 3–5 years in a role where you owned client outcomes — customer success, solutions engineering, implementation consulting, technical account management, or AEO/SEO delivery at an agency or SaaS company. You didn’t just maintain relationships; you drove measurable results, coordinated across teams, and were accountable for whether things actually moved.
You understand the fundamentals of how search and AI-driven discovery work. You know what structured data is, why schema markup matters, how Google Search Console and GA4 connect to organic traffic, and what makes a page machine-readable versus invisible to crawlers. You don’t need to write code — but you need to write a brief that a developer can execute without a follow-up call.
Beyond the experience, what matters is:
You think in systems, not tasks. You don’t just deliver a set of fixes — you understand which fixes move which outcomes, how on-site and off-site work compounds, and how monitoring data connects to the client’s commercial results. You see the whole loop.
You’re consultative and data-led. When a client asks what to prioritize this month, you answer with monitoring data, not intuition. You can translate a brand’s poor visibility on non-branded queries into a commercial story about lost consideration share, and then specify the exact fixes that close the gap.
You coordinate across teams without authority. You’ll brief agencies, dev teams, PR teams, and community managers — none of whom report to you. You get things done through clarity of the brief, strength of the evidence, and the quality of your working relationships.
You write clearly and precisely. Most of your work is written — strategy briefs, fix specifications, content briefs, Loom walkthroughs, client updates. When you specify a technical fix, the team implementing it doesn’t have to guess what you mean.
You spot automation opportunities. When you do the same thing manually across five clients, your instinct is to flag it as an automation candidate. You think about where AI tools and agentic workflows can replace repetitive work — and you bring specific suggestions, not vague complaints.

Bonus: Experience in AEO, GEO, or SEO delivery. Background at a digital marketing agency, martech company, or SaaS platform in a client-facing delivery role. Familiarity with schema markup, structured data, and technical SEO concepts.

WHAT’S HARD ABOUT THIS ROLE
You’re managing 10–15 accounts simultaneously, each running multiple product layers, each with their own agencies or internal teams and stakeholder dynamics. The operational load is high. If you’ve only managed 2–3 accounts at a time, this will be a step change.
You coordinate, you don’t control. You write the briefs and specifications, but the client’s dev team deploys the schema, the client’s PR agency places the articles, the client’s community team responds on Reddit. When things don’t get done, you escalate with data and persistence, not authority.
The category is new. Most clients are learning AI visibility alongside you. You’ll need to educate while you deliver — and sometimes the client’s team won’t prioritize your fixes because they don’t yet understand why they matter for AI engines. You make the case clearly and repeatedly.
Evening calls are part of the job. Not every day, but US clients need live time. Expect 1–3 evenings a week. If you want a strict 9-to-6, this won’t work.

WHAT YOU GET
₹12–15 LPA fixed — based on experience and calibration during the process.
₹3–5 LPA variable — tied to client retention and net revenue expansion.
₹3–5 LPA in ESOPs — real equity in a company building infrastructure for AI commerce.
Total CTC: ₹18–25 LPA (fixed + variable + equity).

Founding delivery seat. You’re building the client delivery function from scratch. The path from here is Lead Brand Engineer → Head of Client Success as the company scales.
Full-stack client ownership. You run strategy, write briefs, QA outputs, coordinate implementation, track outcomes, and drive expansion — across the full stack from monitoring to on-site to off-site to authority. This is end-to-end ownership that most CS roles at larger companies never offer.
Front seat to a market being built. AI is rewriting how buyers discover and choose products. You’ll work with brands across categories and see first-hand how AI engines represent (or misrepresent) each one — the technical gaps, the off-site narrative patterns, the citation structures that determine who gets recommended. The knowledge you build about AI-mediated commerce doesn’t exist in any textbook. You’ll help define the playbooks, fix taxonomies, and engagement frameworks that shape how the industry thinks about AI visibility. Within 6 months you’ll understand this space better than most people working in it.
AI tools as daily infrastructure. You’ll use ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools as core workflow — for brand research, brief writing, output QA, pattern recognition, and client communication. You’ll upskill faster here than in any structured training program.
Direct influence on the product. Your Voice of Customer briefs and automation suggestions directly shape what gets built. You don’t file tickets into a void — you talk to the founder and things change.
